maria_garcia: FYI p99 spike on hosted API for tenant-42 starting ~18:12 UTC, p99 ~2.1s -> 5.6s. Not steady — correlated with short-chat burst pattern. Queue depth climbed to 420 on the front-end LB.
aj_singh: seeing same. rate limiter counters show tenant-42 burst at ~6k rps for ~3m then dropped. backlog metrics: pending_requests peaked 420, active_workers at capacity 128 per pool.
ryan_c: initial flamegraph looks like KV cache churn. eviction_count for kvcache pool increased 14x during spike. suspect aggressive eviction + small seq length causing lots of rewarm.
leila_ops: noisy tenant is a third-party app integration kicking off thousands of 1-3 token completion requests. They say it's a load-test. I asked them to scale back but need mitigation now.
aj_singh: quick mitigation options: 1) apply soft throttling to tenant-42 in RL layer; 2) increase kvcache max_entries for hosted-pool-3; 3) pin kernel selection to large-batch kernel for that pool to avoid oscillation. Thoughts?
ryan_c: kernel selection oscillation is interesting — our heuristic flips between small-seq optimized kernel and generic kernel based on instantaneous seq distribution. With lots of tiny requests queued behind long ones, the heuristic flips and we pay warm-up cost repeatedly.
maria_garcia: can you paste profiler output?
perf-bot: attached snapshot id perf-4371 (sampling window 18:14-18:17).
ryan_c: paste: ```
# top callers
kernel_select()                        34.2%  (context switch cost spikes)
kv_cache::evict_entry()                19.8%
executor::dispatch_request()           12.1%
attention::matmul_shard()              8.7%
memory::alloc_retry()                  7.6%
# kv cache counters
kv_hits: 12.4%   kv_misses: 87.6%
evictions: 14,200  readds: 13,900  rewarm_time_avg_ms: 4.8
# backlog
frontend_queue_len: 420
worker_pool_queue: 320
avg_worker_idle: 0.6% (starved)
```
aj_singh: looks like rewarm_time_avg is tiny but frequency is huge. Combined with kernel_select churn we're thrashing both cache and kernel choice. That increases tail latency even though per-op time is small.
leila_ops: I can limit tenant to 800 rps for 15m. Shall I proceed? :warning:
aj_singh: yes please. Also schedule a targeted config change: bump kvcache entries from 50k->80k for hosted-pool-3 for next 30m and enable sticky kernel override for that pool: `kernel_policy: prefer_stable`
maria_garcia: how risky is kernel override?
ryan_c: low risk short term — it forces kernel_select to pick the stable large-batch kernel. Perf diff: at steady-state small-seq latency goes up ~5-8% but removes oscillation. TL;DR: reduces p99 under thrash.
sre-oncall: I'm applying a temporary rate limit to tenant-42 (800 rps windowed) and toggling kvcache entries now. Will update infra events.
perf-bot: action_log: {"rate_limit_applied":"tenant-42","kvcache_bumped":"hosted-pool-3","kernel_override":"hosted-pool-3:prefer_stable","operator":"sre-oncall","ts":"1802003498"}
aj_singh: after changes we should watch these metrics: p95/p99, kv_miss_rate, eviction_rate, kernel_switch_rate, worker_queue_len. Set alerts for kernel_switch_rate > 5/min.
maria_garcia: observed p99 drop from 5.6s -> 1.9s within 2m of mitigation. backlog reduced to ~60.
leila_ops: tenant confirmed they paused load test. :thumbsup:
ryan_c: root cause write-up draft: noisy tenant burst of many tiny completions caused KV-cache evictions and kernel-selection oscillation. Combined effect amplified tail latency due to rewarm and kernel warm-up. Short-term fixes: tenant throttling, kvcache capacity bump, kernel policy override. Mid-term: change kernel selection heuristic to incorporate recent cache-eviction churn signal and add per-tenant small-request shaping.
maria_garcia: assign follow-ups: aj to own heuristic fix, ryan to add cache-churn metric + dashboard, leila to update tenant policy docs. ETA 2d for triage fixes.
aj_singh: ack. starting a small PR to add a cooldown to kernel selection when eviction_rate > threshold. Will tag reviewers.
sre-oncall: closing incident thread — reopen if p99 climbs again.
